title: A direct line to your Wahoo rides.
summary: Bring your Wahoo cycling history into RideVector, with no Strava account required.

changes.title: Connect with Wahoo
changes.text: Authorize read-only access to your Wahoo profile and workouts in Connections. Import completed cycling workouts directly, including distance, climbing, active timer duration, and available sensor averages.

changes.title: Make room for your history
changes.text: Import up to 30 workouts per request, then continue with Import older rides. Reimports update the same source recording; matching Strava and file recordings count once. Wahoo does not return workouts originating in third-party apps.

changes.title: Your files still come along
changes.text: Upload original FIT files for route maps and sensor graphs, or for history unavailable through Wahoo. Wahoo imports run when you press Import; background syncing is not enabled. Disconnect revokes Wahoo access and retains previously imported rides, which you can remove individually.

changes.title: A clearer import result
changes.text: Wahoo imports check individual cycling workouts when the list omits completed results. Import messages distinguish entries without completed results, non-cycling workouts, and missing ride fields.

changes.title: One day, one update
changes.text: Same-day releases now share a single card. Search, filters, sharing, older direct links, and interactive previews stay available.

changes.title: Take the features for a spin
changes.text: Try sample Wahoo imports and duplicate grouping without signing in. Preview your own FIT, GPX, TCX, or CSV files locally in a temporary workspace; nothing is uploaded or saved.

daily.title: More ways in. More to explore.
daily.summary: A direct Wahoo connection, flexible file imports, and a release journal you can take for a spin. All of today’s improvements, together.

title: Good things deserve a place to land.
summary: Meet the RideVector release journal: a closer look at the little improvements and bigger adventures happening here.

changes.title: Your release journal
changes.text: Explore shipped features, improvements, and fixes in one place, with links from the dashboard.

changes.title: Find your next discovery
changes.text: Search updates, filter by change type, expand the details, or copy a direct link to a release. Interactive examples let you explore selected features with sample data.

changes.title: A living record
changes.text: Release notes are now part of RideVector’s update workflow, with a repository check that flags product changes missing a release-note update.

title: More ways in. More miles ahead.
summary: Your riding history should come along for the journey. Bring your files, skip the Strava requirement, and keep every ride in perspective.

changes.title: FIT files, welcome aboard
changes.text: Import recorded cycling sessions with available GPS, heart-rate, and power data. Device timer duration is shown separately from elapsed and moving time.

changes.title: Bring the whole riding story
changes.text: Select up to 100 FIT, GPX, TCX, or CSV files in one batch: up to 10 MB per file, 50 MB combined, and 2,000 rides. Individual file failures are reported so you can retry.

changes.title: One ride, counted once
changes.text: Confidently matched recordings from different sources count once while original source copies stay saved. Manual entries and uncertain matches stay separate. Manage the grouping in Connections.

changes.title: Strava is optional
changes.text: Continue without Strava is now prominent in onboarding. A RideVector account, your activity files, or manual ride entry are enough to get started.

title: A riding week that moves with you.
summary: Plans are useful. Plans that leave room for real life are better. Your coach now puts riding time, recent effort, and recovery in the picture.

changes.title: Your plans, in Apple Calendar
changes.text: Create a private, revocable calendar subscription for saved training sessions and races. It’s a one-way feed; your calendar app controls refresh timing.

changes.title: Time comes first
changes.text: Coach drafts use recent riding minutes, consistency, recovery check-ins, and usable cached power or heart-rate evidence. Distance stays a secondary estimate.

changes.title: Room for the week you actually had
changes.text: Future, unedited adaptive coach sessions can adjust as RideVector refreshes, imports rides, or receives a check-in. Personal edits and completed or past sessions stay protected. Missed riding isn’t turned into catch-up work.

changes.title: Clearer coaching context
changes.text: Coach wording now distinguishes adaptive sessions from personal plans and handles stale account loads more carefully. Training suggestions remain transparent planning heuristics, not readiness predictions.

title: A little structure. A clear next step.
summary: From the next easy spin to your next start line, keep your riding plans, race days, and personal progress together.

changes.title: Make room for your next adventure
changes.text: A private training calendar brings recorded rides, planned sessions, rest days, and races into one view. Weekly recaps and personal records put your history in perspective.

changes.title: Your next start line
changes.text: Save races, including multi-day events, and create editable weekly coach drafts around your availability and race goals.

changes.title: Power and heart-rate zones
changes.text: Save your FTP and heart-rate boundaries, then explore estimated time in zones from available ride recordings. Missing sensor data stays visible as missing.

changes.title: A smoother Strava connection
changes.text: Private-activity permission is optional, connection failures give actionable explanations, and scope parsing accepts comma- or space-separated permissions.

daily.title: Your next start line starts here.
daily.summary: A private home for your riding history, training calendar, race plans, and personal zones. The first miles of RideVector, in one daily update.

title: Every riding story starts somewhere.
summary: The first RideVector dashboard: a private home for your rides, the miles you’re putting in, and the adventures still ahead.

changes.title: Your rides, your rhythm
changes.text: Private accounts, ride uploads, manual entries, and an optional Strava connection bring your cycling history together.

changes.title: A little perspective
changes.text: Explore five date ranges, weekly goals, route maps, available sensor graphs, and duration-based Fitness and Fatigue trends. Distances display in miles and elevation in feet.

changes.title: Comfort in every light
changes.text: Responsive layouts and a persistent light/dark theme make the dashboard feel at home on your screen.
